title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 36
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • A new format for the Community Wishlist is open for feedback. You can read the proposed ideas on Meta. This new process plans to improve how wishes are triaged, voted on, and prioritized in a way that is transparent and balanced across project families and language editions. This consultation is open for two weeks.

    • Updates for editors

  • The latest release of the Wikipedia Android app includes updates to the Saved feature, bringing the app’s saving experience closer to iOS and Web. The update redesigns the Saved tab with an “All articles” view, removes the default “Saved” reading list, renames reading lists to “Collections,” and modernizes the article-saving experience. [1]

title: Coordinate Me – The World’s Largest Wikidata Competition
content:
The third edition of the international Wikidata competition Coordinate Me 2026 has concluded with remarkable results, setting new records for community engagement and data enrichment on the platform. The circumstances remain unchanged from previous years: the competition was organized by Wikimedia Österreich and ran throughout May 2026 and brought together Wikidata editors from around the globe to improve and create geolocatable content.

The 2026 edition proved to be the most successful yet, with participants editing over 1 million items, setting yet another record for the competition after last year’s successful second edition. What makes this achievement particularly noteworthy is that 719 newly registered users joined the platform specifically for this event. This significant influx of newcomers was supported by introductory workshops in multiple languages, four of which were organized by Wikimedia Österreich, ensuring that new editors received proper guidance rather than being left to navigate the complexities of Wikidata alone, thus increasing the likelihood of newcomer retention.

title: A Week to Remember: Bridges Across Borders at WikiCamp 2026
content:
Summer International Youth WikiCamp 2026—perhaps this title alone is enough to convey the immense work, energy, and dedication poured into just seven days. Yet, this post is about more than just the accomplished work. It is about friendship, structure, responsibility, and, of course, the endless possibilities of Wiki.

During this WikiCamp, I—Argam Hakobyan—served as a Wiki-аssistant. For those who might not know what a Wiki-аssistant is, let me explain briefly. At WikiCamp, participants are usually divided into four or five groups, each with its dedicated Wiki-аssistant. The assistant’s main role is to guide participants during editing workshops, help them navigate article editing, correct mistakes, and review their progress. This is arguably one of the most responsible roles at the camp, as the participants’ progress and final outcomes depend heavily on the assistant’s support.

title: FY25-26 Annual Funding Programs Reflections & Learnings
content:
Every year, the Community Resources team shares reflections and learnings from our primary community funding programs: Rapid and General Support Funds. Our goal in sharing these reflections is to highlight and celebrate the volunteers and affiliates who sustain our movement, and to provide clear visibility into how our funding is being used. Read on for a transparent look at our FY27 grants budget, our priorities for the year, and the renewal of our grants strategy.

Over the 2025–2026 funding year, we supported 427 grants totalling $17.73 million across 90 countries, with 56.2% of funds distributed outside North America and Northern & Western Europe. Facing global economic turbulence, inflation, and volatile currency shifts, our Regional Funding Committees leaned into fiscal discipline while continuing to champion equity; growing active multi-year commitments to 47 and pushing decision-making closer to the communities through localised funding models like the Nigeria National Funding Initiative, CEE Rapid Fund Program, Wiki in Africa Campaigns, and the Wikimedia Colombia Hacerwiki 2026.

title: Wikimedia Residencies at UTDT: A WIR Experience from an Educational Program
content:
The WMAR education program is carrying out its first initiative to support Wikimedians in Residence (WIR). In this post, we will tell you about this initiative and how it is progressing.

The role of the WIR is widely recognized within the Wikimedia Movement, especially within GLAM programs or institutions. A Wikimedian in Residence (WIR) is a person who serves as a liaison between the institution to which they belong (museum, library, university) and the local Wikimedia chapter in their country. In this link, the WIR’s role is to implement open knowledge projects within the institution, such as digitization efforts, research, talks, or editing workshops.

title: “The people made me stay” – Meet Mari Avetisyan, the Wikimedian of the Year
content:
Mari’s Wikimedia journey began when a shy university student joined a WikiCamp, unsure whether she belonged. Today, she works at Wikimedia Armenia, contributes to Armenian Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, and Wikidata, serves as Chair of the Affiliations Committee, and supports Wikimedia initiatives at local, regional, and global levels. Recently recognized with a Wikimedian of the Year Honorary Award, she reflects on her unexpected path from hesitant volunteer to community leader, the importance of confidence and support, and the lessons she has learned along the way. For Mari, young people should not be viewed only as the movement’s next generation: we need to make space for them now and include them equally in shaping Wikimedia’s present and future.

To start, could you tell us a bit about yourself, and how your journey with the Wikimedia movement first began back in 2018?

M: I’m Mari, a Wikimedian from Armenia who joined the movement in 2018. Since then, Wikimedia has become both a big part of my professional life and a community that I feel deeply connected to. I work at Wikimedia Armenia and, in my free time, contribute to Armenian Wikipedia, Wikimedia Commons, and Wikidata.

title: From Lens to Legacy: WikiCommons PH Con 2027 heads to Puerto Princesa City
content:
PhilWiki Community has announced that next Wikimedia Commons Philippines Conference will be held from April 16 to 18, 2027 in Puerto Princesa City, Palawan, bringing together Wikimedia Commons contributors, Wiki Loves Philippines campaign winners and participants, photographers, and open knowledge advocates from across the Philippines.

As one of PhilWiki Community’s flagship initiatives, the Philippine WikiConference serves as a central platform for community engagement, knowledge exchange, capacity building, and partnership development. The annual gathering provides opportunities for volunteers, cultural institutions, educators, and heritage advocates to collaborate in advancing free and open knowledge.

The local community has chosen the theme From Lens to Legacy, highlighting how photographs and multimedia can contribute to preserving collective memory. “Images captured by the lens and learnings from the Commons conference will become part of legacy. Legacy encompasses history, language, culture, memory, the environment/biodiversity, and whatever we have in our repositories. Such legacy can be shared locally and globally,” expounded WikiConference director Bernadette Roco.

title: Keizo Shibusawa and Collective Intelligence: the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture Edit-a-thon
content:
On August 25, 2026, I contributed in an edit-a-thon held at the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture, Kanagawa University. The Institute collects and organizes folk artifacts and historical documents from across Japan and conducts research focusing on the society of ordinary Japanese people—including the history of the fishing industry.

The roots of the Institute lie in the Attic Museum Society, founded by Keizo Shibusawa in 1921; this organization later became the Attic Museum and was renamed the Institute for the Study of Japanese Folk Culture in 1942, during the war. Although Shibusawa took over the management of Dai-Ichi Bank at the request of his grandfather, Eiichi Shibusawa, and subsequently served as Governor of the Bank of Japan and Minister of Finance at the government’s request during and after the war. However, as he had originally aspired to a life of scholarship, he poured his passion into training many researchers, starting with folklorists.

title: Wikipedia, Digital Literacy, and Science Communication among High School Students in Brazil: Introducing NEMkipédiA
content:
On November 30, 2024, Wikimedia Brasil (WMB) participated in the VII Encontro Anual da Rede Nacional de Ciência para Educação (Rede CpE) (7th Annual Meeting of the National Science for Education Network). The event celebrated the tenth anniversary of the Rede CpE, an initiative that brings together researchers from different fields of knowledge to share scientific studies that contribute to better educational practices and policies. That year, the event also included the III Simpósio Satélite da Cátedra UNESCO de Ciência para Educação (3rd Satellite Symposium of the UNESCO Chair in Science for Education) as part of its program.

As a result of our participation, we received an honorable mention for the research we presented, titled Wikiversidade: uma plataforma para grupos de pesquisa e ciência aberta (Wikiversity: A Platform for Research Groups and Open Science). The study investigated the challenges and opportunities of Wikiversity for Brazilian scientific production and dissemination and was based on an article published on Wikiversity.

title: From Slovenia to Armenia: A WikiCamp, a Peer Exchange, and New Connections
content:
The Wikimedia movement is built on collaboration, sharing experiences, and learning from one another. So when the CEE Hub announced its Peer Learning Exchange, Wikimedia Armenia was excited to take part.

The idea of the exchange was simple: bring a developing Wikimedia community closer to a more established one, creating an opportunity to learn from each other’s experiences, share best practices, and build connections that could continue beyond the exchange itself.

Our exchange brought us together with Nal Mencin from the Wikipedians of Slovenia User Group. Once we started discussing what the exchange could look like, one activity immediately stood out: Wikimedia Armenia’s Summer Youth WikiCamp.

The WikiCamp seemed like the perfect opportunity for Nal to experience our community from the inside. Rather than simply observing how we work, we wanted him to become part of it. So, the exchange combined meetings and discussions with the Wikimedia Armenia team with something much more hands-on: becoming a WikiCamp participant.

From the very beginning, we wanted Nal to experience the WikiCamp not as an observer, but as a real participant.

title: Bridging Access: Mapping Maternal and Child Health Facilities in Ikwerre LGA, Rivers State
content:
Access to reliable health information does not begin and end in a hospital. Sometimes, it begins with simply knowing where a health facility is, what it looks like, and that it exists. In Ikwerre Local Government Area (LGA) of Rivers State, Nigeria, maternal and child health facilities play an important role in providing essential healthcare to women, children, and families. Yet, information about many of these facilities remains poorly documented and difficult to find online.

This gap inspired “Bridging Access: Mapping Maternal and Child Health Facilities in Ikwerre LGA, Rivers State,” a Wikimedia project designed to make local health facilities more visible through photography, structured data, and community participation. The project brought together Wikimedia contributors and participants to document maternal and child health facilities across Ikwerre LGA and contribute this information to Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata.

title: Wikidata #2 workshop held in Tokyo, Japan
content:
We held a workshop about Wikidata in the Tokyo Metropolitan Library in Meguro district on August 22nd. This was the second event related to Wikidata organized by the Wikimedians of Japan User Group. 21 people have participated, comprising a diverse group of residents of both the Kansai and Kanto regions, ranging from beginners to experienced veteran editors.

This workshop was spearheaded by a member of Open Knowledge Japan forum Higashi Shusaku. First he explained what Wikidata is and how to edit it, then we continued into a hands-on practical session. Following a pre-prepared list of incomplete or missing entries, we all dove into the editing process.

We were joined by some truly inspiring people, including Eugene Ormandy, a Wikimedian of the Year 2023 nominee, and Hijiri, this year’s Honorable Mention nominee. Seeing that even such experienced editors still have things to learn was a huge motivation for the rest of us to keep learning.
snippet: We held a workshop about Wikidata in the Tokyo Metropolitan Library in Meguro district on August 22nd. This was the second event related to Wikidata organized by the Wikimedians of Japan User Group.

title: The Yurakaré people and the Wikimedia movement
content: For a few years now, Wikimedistas de Bolivia has been working with representatives of Indigenous nations to put together open educational resources about the different languages spoken in the country. This year, the Bolivian user group got in touch with the Institute of Language and Culture of the Yurakaré Nation (ILC-NY) and invited its members to create an illustrated alphabet of their language and upload it to Wikimedia Commons. What we’d like is for Commons to eventually have open educational resources for all of Bolivia’s languages, available for anyone to download and use freely. That said, reaching out to the institutions in charge of safeguarding Indigenous languages in the country isn’t always straightforward, and it usually takes a long time.
